scope: Focused final integration review after round-two transport, availability, error-provenance, phase-panic and native response-identity fixes. Broker/relay findings were implemented by this reviewing workstream and are not represented as an independent audit of its own changes.
verified_behaviors: Automatic initialization first loads S3; only explicit absence without an expected identity pin reaches generation and conditional create. Errors and pinned missing storage cannot replace the seed. Signing algorithms and mint-burn custody behavior stay unchanged.

Phase reservation releases the mutex before external custody I/O; failed/expired recovery cannot activate. Read-only swap callback unwind drops the phase guard before resuming the panic, preventing poisoning. Production panic=abort is unchanged.
Custody uses absolute shrinking deadlines; late conditional PUT completion is recovered by the next load. Broker retains AWS-operation slots until the actual worker exits.

Broker authorizes kernel peer CIDs before reads, caps each CID at four connections/two AWS workers, and limits dispatch to four operations/sec with burst eight. One create performs at most one PUT and one GET with SDK retries disabled. Worker-start failure releases quotas and keeps accepting.

KMS relay guard rejects wrong socket families/local endpoints/peer CIDs before subprocesses. systemd admission applies per-source CID quotas and socat receives only a literal regional destination and clean environment. Per-instance/aggregate resources and a hard service lifetime are bounded.

Swap forwarders use four workers, four copy threads and eight queued connections per listener. Queue/connect/copy share an acceptance deadline; nonblocking VSOCK connect has a two-second cap. Errors close both directions; EOF retains response delivery. Non-swap transport remains on its prior path.

Broker and native helper return fixed category envelopes/statuses; Rust maps only known categories to retryability. Raw AWS or host error messages, credentials and seed values never enter those diagnostics.

Native output is bound to the authoritative KMS response KeyId before and after the official SDK parser. Strict flat input counts reject duplicate members; session-token absence remains valid for long-lived IAM credentials.

The maintained SDK lifecycle patch remains byte-identical and reproducibly bound to its upstream commit. TLS, SigV4, attestation and CMS use official implementations. Deployment approval compares actual EIF measurements and measured public configuration.

retained_sdk_evidence.notes: The SDK patch and its regression bytes match retained proofs. Native helper main.c changed in this round; current helper/E2E/EIF evidence is recorded separately, not claimed source-identical to the old helper.

residuals: Separate upstream connection-setup completion can lose an early notification; the helper 12-second limit bounds the availability failure and fails initialization closed.

An unpinned identity cannot authenticate existing same-context ciphertext against a dishonest broker. Pin the independently verified identity and retire generation authority before funding; verify backup restore.

Allowed CID access grants the full dedicated instance role. CID reuse does not prove image identity; KMS recipient attestation and narrow IAM enforce custody. Quotas do not prevent the parent from stopping enclaves or exhausting unrelated host resources.

Inherited conditional webpki and optional Helios dependency matches remain documented in REMEDIATION.md. Cargo/NSM/pip coordinates are unchanged. Parent systemd/socat are maintained distro packages outside that saved package query; see the host dependency scope.
Live AWS/Nitro policy enforcement, real parent VSOCK socket activation/cgroup admission and production backup recovery remain deployment checks.
